subject: Hosted quickstart — sandbox endpoints, throttle proposal & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Kayla Rhodes <kayla@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted quickstart — sandbox endpoints, throttle proposal & next steps

Hi Kayla — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

What we covered
- Demo: chat + retrieval flow, embeddings for semantic search, basic rate behavior in sandbox.
- Integration touches: completions/chat endpoint, embeddings, auth + IP allowlist.
- Top concern you raised: whether Hosted keeps you within latency and cost targets and how quickly Ledgerly can run a small pilot.

What I propose for a hosted quickstart (pilot)
1) Sandbox access: provision a sandbox API key + dedicated sandbox endpoints (non-prod) so you can run integration/QA.
2) Pilot ratecap: start with a conservative default of 20 requests/sec sustained, burst to 80 rps for short periods. We can raise this after baseline telemetry.
3) Token guidance: default per-request token cap = 2,500 tokens. If your average prompt/response is larger we can exchange numbers and set token-based quotas.
4) Security: IP allowlisting + optional VPC peering later (if you decide to move to Private).

Questions for you
- Do you want us to provision sandbox with 20 rps sustained / 80 rps burst, or start higher (example: 50 rps sustained)?
- Typical input size (avg tokens in prompt + expected reply tokens)? This helps us size KV cache and advise batching.
- Any hard constraints on data residency or contract terms we should prep for?

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (recording), redwood-sandbox-ops-sheet.pdf (ops checklist)

Next steps
- If you sign off on the pilot config I’ll loop in Marissa to provision the sandbox and send a short ops checklist + schedule a technical onboarding (30m).
- I’ll also attach a short SOW/standard SLA for your legal to glance at.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow call if helpful.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Kayla Rhodes <kayla@ledgerly.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-14T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted quickstart — sandbox endpoints, throttle proposal & next steps

Thanks Sergio — appreciate the clear recap and the recording. A few quick answers and follow-ups below:

1) Deployment mode: for the initial pilot we want Hosted — faster to stand up and evaluate. We may revisit Dedicated or Private later if we need stronger guarantees or VPC network isolation.
2) Expected traffic for pilot: ~30 rps sustained spread across several user sessions, with spikes up to ~120 rps during peak tests. Production expectations TBD but could be 200–300 rps over time.
3) Typical prompt sizes: short user queries (~40–80 tokens) plus retrieval + assistant reply averaging 200–300 tokens. So plan for ~350 tokens/request as a starting point.
4) Security: IP allowlisting is required for the sandbox. Data residency — we’re US-based, no EU constraint for now.

Specific asks:
- Can the sandbox be opened to 100 rps sustained (or at least 50 rps) for a 2-week stress window? We want to run concurrency tests.
- Is there a limit on concurrent KV cache entries / session affinity we should be aware of?

If you can provision sandbox credentials and an ops checklist today/tonight I’ll forward to our infra engineer to start smoke tests.

— Kayla
Product Lead, Ledgerly
kayla@ledgerly.com

> Hi Kayla — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum:...

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kayla Rhodes <kayla@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2025-05-14T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted quickstart — sandbox endpoints, throttle proposal & next steps

Looping you both — Ledgerly wants Hosted for the pilot and is asking for a sandbox that can hit up to 100 rps sustained (ideally) for a short stress window. They estimate ~350 tokens/request.

Ask: can we provision a sandbox instance with the following defaults?
- Sandbox key + non-prod endpoints
- Initial pilot throttle: 50 rps sustained, burst to 200 rps for short windows OR option to open 100 rps sustained for a 2-week stress window.
- Token cap: 3,000 tokens/request safety ceiling.
- IP allowlist enabled for their infra team.

Marissa — can you confirm the quickest way to enable this and whether there’s any internal approval needed for the temporary 100 rps sustained window? Chloe — can you draft the ops checklist (short) with the endpoints we should hand Ledgerly?

I’ll coordinate the onboarding call once we confirm quotas.

— Sergio

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kayla Rhodes <kayla@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2025-05-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted quickstart — sandbox endpoints, throttle proposal & next steps

Thanks for the tag, Sergio. Quick ops response below — copying the checklist attachment (redwood-sandbox-ops-sheet.pdf).

Provisioning notes
- We can create a dedicated sandbox API key and sandbox endpoints for Ledgerly within 24 hours.
- Default sandbox quota: 50 rps sustained; burst allowed to 200 rps for short bursts.
- For the 2-week stress window we can temporarily raise sustained quota to 100 rps with a short approvals path (Ops lead + Prod infra sign-off). I’ll start that approval flow if you confirm.

Token / caching guidance
- With ~350 tokens/request we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching on retrieval-heavy flows; this usually reduces token bill and improves tail latency.
- Token cap: we’ll set request max to 3,000 tokens to be safe.

Security & endpoints
- IP allowlist: yes — provide the CIDR blocks from Ledgerly’s infra team and we’ll lock the sandbox key.
- Endpoints to hand off (examples): POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions, POST https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

Ops deliverables we’ll send
1) redwood-sandbox-ops-sheet.pdf (small checklist + endpoints) — attached.
2) short onboarding 30m call invite (I can propose times).
3) standard-sla.pdf (for legal reference) — will attach to the outbound email after Sergio confirms.

Next steps
- Sergio: confirm that Ledgerly wants the temporary 100 rps sustained window for a 2-week stress run and I’ll kick the approval flow.
- Kayla: please send the CIDR ranges to lock the key once you have them.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference

Kayla — great, thanks for the details and confirming Hosted for the pilot. Summary & next steps below: 

What we’ll provision (timeline: within 24 hours once you confirm CIDR)
- Dedicated sandbox API key + endpoints (non-prod).
- Baseline quota: 50 rps sustained, burst to 200 rps. We’ll open a temporary 2-week window at 100 rps sustained if you confirm you’d like the stress run.
- Request token cap set to 3,000 tokens.
- IP allowlist: we’ll lock the sandbox key to the CIDR(s) you provide.

Immediate asks for Ledgerly
- Confirm whether you want the temporary 100 rps sustained window for the stress tests (yes/no).
- Send CIDR blocks for IP allowlisting.

Logistics
- I’ve linked the HubSpot deal here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-9876 and attached standard-sla.pdf for legal review.

If that all looks good I’ll have Marissa provision the sandbox and Chloe will share the ops checklist and endpoints. Thanks — excited to get Ledgerly running.
